offer.name: An AI operating system
offer.body: One layer that knows your business: its documents, processes, clients and prices. It’s connected to the tools your team already uses, so anyone can ask it something or hand it work, and it acts inside those tools.

offer.name: Agents
offer.body: An agent owns one job from start to finish: answering inquiries, following up leads, chasing invoices, preparing the weekly report. It works in your tools and hands anything unusual to a person.

offer.name: Agent swarms
offer.body: Several agents passing work between them, for jobs with stages. One takes the request, one researches, one drafts, one checks, and a person approves where it matters.

path.name: The Intake
path.promise: Nine questions, and my first read while you wait.
points: What the business does, the tools you use, and what eats your week
A prognosis on the spot: what I’d build, where I’d start, and what I’d ask you
A call booked from the same page, or the conversation carried on by email

path.name: The Map
path.promise: How the work actually moves today.
points: I talk to you and the people who do the work
Every step, tool and handoff in the jobs worth handing over, written down
A plan for what to build first, and what to leave with people

path.name: The Build
path.promise: Systems made for your business, in your tools.
points: The operating system, the agents, or both, built from the map
Connected to the tools you already use, with your documents and processes behind them
A person approves anything that matters, until you decide otherwise

path.name: The Rollout
path.promise: Your team using it, not working around it.
points: Launched one job at a time, so nothing changes all at once
Your team shown how to work with it
Adjusted on what real use shows

path.name: The Keep
path.when: Every month, if you want it
path.promise: It keeps up as the business changes.
points: New jobs added as you find them
Checks on what the agents did, and fixes when something drifts
A monthly look at what it handled and where it got stuck

proof.quote: 70,000 hours is not an abstraction. That’s real people, real shifts, and real time that was going to paperwork and is now going back to our teammates.
Before this transformational tech, teams of people spent over half the day chasing missed pickups – manually checking carrier websites, making calls, recording updates and notifying customers.
ChatGPT Work runs this report for me every morning. It finds all the inconsistencies all the way across the internet, so I can ensure all of this information is correct.
It knows who we are. It knows where we came from. It knows where we want to go.

cases.name: WellNest
cases.title: WellNest: a free UX teardown of a Base44 app
cases.summary: A health tracker for people living with chronic illness, built in Base44. Its founder asked for feedback on Reddit, so I sent a free teardown.

before.alt: WellNest’s homepage before: floating cards cover the paragraph, a waitlist sits under the main button, and two “FREE” pills sit beside the price. Each is marked with a red number.
before.caption: Before · the teardown, numbered to match the fixes below

after.alt: WellNest’s homepage after: the floating cards sit clear of the text, one line explains the price, and the trial is the only sign-up.
after.caption: After · the same screen, once the fixes were live

fixes.found: On a laptop, the floating preview cards landed on the headline and the paragraph.
fixes.shipped: The cards moved to the sides, clear of the text.

fixes.found: A waitlist for a feature that wasn’t out yet sat right under the main button.
fixes.shipped: The free trial is the only sign-up on the first screen.

fixes.found: Two “FREE” pills beside “From AU$4.99/month” left people guessing what was free.
fixes.shipped: One plain line: free for 7 days, then AU$4.99 a month.

fixes.found: The link for people managing more than one condition was dark green on near-black, at 1.9:1 contrast.
fixes.shipped: Light text at 14:1. Readable text needs 4.5:1.

fixes.found: In the free preview, the pain slider started at 5 but said “Not selected”, so tapping 5 did nothing.
